title: MRTS submodule update can execute forked code
description: The only code change is the MRTS submodule pointer, moving tools/MRTS from 13aa91291adea12d5c607fdd165d010fcfb1da78 to 13e6aefebe1dd2179f8b44b6d9eea67e64325316. The configured submodule remote is a personal fork, not the official owasp-modsecurity/MRTS repository. When MRTS support is used, the framework runs tools/MRTS/mrts/generate-rules.py directly with Python. The generated output is then imported into framework cases, and the importer hard-codes the origin repo as owasp-modsecurity/MRTS. This means the submodule revision changed by this commit is an executable supply-chain dependency: a malicious MRTS submodule revision can run arbitrary Python on any runner or developer machine that initializes the submodule and invokes MRTS targets, while generated cases can be represented as official MRTS-derived material. Default GitHub Actions checkouts set submodules: false, which reduces direct PR-CI reachability, so this is not critical, but it remains a high-impact supply-chain/code-execution issue for trusted MRTS runs.
relevant_paths: tools/MRTS | gitmodules | ci/provisioning/generate-mrts.sh | ci/lib/mrts-common.sh | Makefile | ci/provisioning/import-mrts-cases.py

title: MRTS submodule redirected to personal fork
description: The changed `.gitmodules` now instructs users and any recursive-submodule automation to fetch `tools/MRTS` from `https://github.com/Easton97-Jens/MRTS.git` instead of the expected `owasp-modsecurity/MRTS` upstream. MRTS is not just passive data: the framework's MRTS generation path executes `tools/MRTS/mrts/generate-rules.py` and imports generated cases. The importer still labels generated cases as originating from `owasp-modsecurity/MRTS`, so content coming from the personal fork can be represented as official OWASP MRTS provenance. The current gitlink commit remains pinned, so a normal `git submodule update --init` cannot be transparently replaced without changing the recorded submodule commit or defeating Git object identity. However, this commit moves the authoritative configured remote to an attacker-controlled namespace, making `--remote` submodule updates, future submodule pointer refreshes, connector CI integrations, or operator workflows that initialize and update MRTS consume code/data from the fork and potentially execute it during MRTS generation.

title: Python updater workflow permits hidden write-token actions
description: The commit adds a scheduled/manual Python updater workflow with a publish job that has contents:write and pull-requests:write. The corresponding checker allow-lists check-python-version.yml for those writes and for token references, then validates only selected substrings and the presence of exactly one create-pull-request step. It does not enforce an exact publish-step allowlist or reject additional uses: steps. Because some already locked actions, notably actions/github-script, can receive github.token via action defaults without an explicit token string in the workflow YAML, a malicious workflow change can add such a pinned action to the publish job and still pass the workflow pin checks, check-ci-security-contract.py, check-python-version.py, and evidence contract checks. After that change is merged, a scheduled/manual run on master would execute the extra action with the job's write-scoped token, bypassing the intended constraint that the publisher only creates a draft PR containing .python-version.

title: Shared /tmp auto-discovery enables smoke cache poisoning
description: The new connector_smoke_default_verified_roots function always adds /tmp/ModSecurity-conector-verified and /var/tmp/ModSecurity-conector-verified search locations, even when those paths were not configured for the current run. find_runtime_binary now searches these shared locations for executable connector runtimes, and connector_smoke_resolve_modsecurity_backend now scans their component-cache directories for libmodsecurity manifests/prefixes. Because /tmp and /var/tmp are shared writable locations on many developer and CI hosts, another local user or a previous untrusted job can pre-create a matching tree such as /tmp/ModSecurity-conector-verified/bin/envoy or /tmp/ModSecurity-conector-verified/component-cache/builds/modsecurity/*/manifest.json with attacker-controlled headers and libmodsecurity.so. A later smoke run can then select and execute/load that artifact without checksum, ownership, or provenance verification. Before this commit, discovery was limited to configured cache/build roots; the new hard-coded shared fallbacks introduce the poisoning path.

title: Lighttpd build trusts staged source and unsafe build paths
description: The new lighttpd build support treats any existing LIGHTTPD_SOURCE_STAGE_DIR as trusted and skips the pinned download and SHA256 verification path. With ALLOW_RUNTIME_BUILDS=1, the script then runs that directory's configure script. The staged source directory is not required to be under the component cache and is not tied to a verified archive, so a poisoned cache or attacker-controlled environment can cause arbitrary code execution in the CI/build account. Separately, LIGHTTPD_BUILD_ROOT is environment-controlled and is deleted with rm -rf. The only under-cache check used for it is a raw string prefix check, so values containing ../ can pass as if they are under CONNECTOR_COMPONENT_CACHE while resolving outside it. This bypasses the intended path restrictions and can delete or recreate directories outside the generated component cache.

title: RESPONSE_BODY report guard now promotes pass-through to PASS
description: RESPONSE_BODY pass-through cases explicitly do not prove that a connector can inspect and block response bodies. Before this commit, those rows were rendered as RESPONSE_BODY_PASS_THROUGH or prefixed non-promoted statuses, and check-response-body-promotion.py rejected any RESPONSE_BODY row that appeared as plain PASS. The commit sets RESPONSE_BODY_PASS_THROUGH_STATUS to PASS, makes response_body_pass_through_status() ignore classification, collapses all pass/fail classifications to plain PASS/FAIL, and removes the plain-PASS checks from the promotion guard. update-runtime-snapshot.py then serializes this computed value as matrix_status. As a result, a normal passing response_body_pass pass-through run, or a malicious connector/runtime summary reporting a RESPONSE_BODY-related case as pass, can be published in runtime matrices as plain PASS even though promotion_allowed remains false and the YAML limitations say pass-through is not blocking proof. This undermines the framework's security-evidence integrity and can create false assurance that a WAF connector supports RESPONSE_BODY enforcement.

title: Ignored files bypass ModSecurity v3 provenance checks
description: The commit adds a full recursive provenance validator for the approved ModSecurity v3 source tree and submodules. Its cleanliness gate uses `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all`, which reports normal untracked files but does not report ignored files unless `--ignored` is also used. The follow-up `git ls-files -v` check only covers tracked index entries. As a result, an attacker who can supply or pre-populate an existing `MODSECURITY_V3_SOURCE_DIR` can keep HEAD, origins, gitdirs, gitlinks, and tracked files at the approved commits while adding ignored files such as stale/generated build outputs. The direct build path then performs `cp -a` of the whole source tree after validation, preserving those ignored files into the build directory. This undermines the new source-provenance boundary because ignored artifacts are not proven to come from the approved commits but can still affect or satisfy the build.

title: RESPONSE_BODY runtime rows are promoted to PASS
description: The changed update-runtime-snapshot.py no longer short-circuits RESPONSE_BODY-related pass results to NOT_EXECUTABLE. After the removal, matrix_status() delegates such rows to matrix_status_for_result(), whose RESPONSE_BODY pass-through status is the literal string PASS. The later non-promotion step adds flags such as response_body_non_verified=true and promotion_allowed=false, but it does not recompute or overwrite matrix_status, and case_matrix_status() only checks flags that were already present in the input summary before those flags are added. As a result, generated runtime snapshots can contain RESPONSE_BODY rows with matrix_status=PASS, which weakens the framework's report-integrity guard against treating RESPONSE_BODY pass-through evidence as verified coverage.

title: Protocol evidence validator allows HTTP/3 fallback flag
description: The protocol evidence validator was changed from a regex-based command policy that explicitly rejected `--http3` to token-based checks. The new forbidden option set omits `--http3`, and `_command_policy_errors` only verifies that the required forced-protocol flag is present. As a result, a command such as `curl --fail-with-body --output /dev/null --http2 --http3 ...` or `curl --fail-with-body --output /dev/null --http3-only --http3 ...` is accepted even though `--http3` is a fallback-capable protocol selector and can contradict or override the intended no-fallback forced protocol profile. This weakens the integrity of H2/H3 protocol evidence and can allow crafted connector/runtime evidence to be treated as valid despite not proving the selected protocol was forced.

title: Workflow checker misses serialized secret contexts
description: The commit introduces ci/checks/security/check-github-actions-workflows.py to enforce the repository's workflow trust boundary. Its secret and github.token detection only matches direct property/index access, such as secrets.FOO, secrets['FOO'], github.token, or github['token']. GitHub Actions expressions can also expose entire contexts, for example ${{ toJSON(secrets) }} or ${{ toJSON(github) }}. Those strings do not match the new regexes, so contains_secret_reference() and contains_github_token_reference() return false. As a result, an unsafe pull_request workflow could place all available secrets into an environment variable, or a workflow/job-level environment could expose the github context including github.token under another name, while the new checker reports success. The currently committed workflows do not contain such a bypass, but the newly introduced security gate has a false negative that can provide false assurance for future workflow changes.

title: Protocol evidence accepts payload-capturing curl commands
description: The commit adds protocol-client evidence validation intended to prove that forced H2/H3 probes are payload-free. However, _validate_command() only checks that the command text contains the substring "--output /dev/null" and uses a regex that only rejects forbidden flags when they are followed by whitespace or end-of-line. A crafted command can therefore include a valid safe-looking output option and then a later overriding option such as "--output /tmp/leaked-body", or use equals-form capture options such as "--dump-header=/tmp/headers" or "--trace-ascii=/tmp/trace". Curl accepts these forms, but the validator does not reject them. Because no_crs_baseline.py copies externally supplied protocol-client artifact bundles into the canonical run and then delegates validation to this checker, a malicious or compromised connector/harness can provide artifacts that pass as managed payload-free evidence while the recorded command would have captured response payloads or headers. This undermines the privacy and integrity guarantees of the new evidence path and can support false protocol PASS claims.

title: Unvalidated engine-version artifact can leak secrets
description: The commit adds full-lifecycle engine sidecar copying. For engine_version, the only content validation is that the source text is non-empty; unlike the digest artifacts, it has no bounded schema, length limit, character allowlist, or forbidden-payload/secret check. The file is then copied verbatim to run_dir/engine-version.txt and added to the manifest. The canonical body-payload/privacy validator scans JSON/JSONL artifacts and .log files under logs/, but not root-level .txt artifacts, so a malicious connector/finalize invocation can place sensitive content such as CI environment data, Authorization headers, or body sentinels into engine-version.txt while validate --check all still succeeds. This undermines the framework's canonical evidence privacy guarantees and can leak secrets if run artifacts are uploaded from CI.

title: No-CRS summary trusts forged PASS result files
description: The introduced summarize path loads each connector's result.json with find_result() and then directly uses the unvalidated status, evidence_stages, capabilities_verified, group_statuses, and status_counts fields to generate JSON and Markdown reports. It does not call validate_run() or require manifest.json, inventory/run.json, results.jsonl, events.jsonl, checksums, PASS gates, or capability consistency before rendering PASS. The Makefile no-crs-summary target invokes this summarizer directly and does not depend on check-no-crs-evidence. As a result, an attacker who can place or alter files under the evidence root, such as a malicious connector harness/repository in CI, can create minimal forged result.json files claiming PASS and have the canonical all-connector report show connector or even overall PASS despite no runtime evidence.

title: Missing HAPROXY_BIN flag enables unsafe binary fallback
description: Before this commit, a non-empty runtime binary variable such as HAPROXY_BIN was treated as authoritative: if the configured path did not exist or was not executable, resolution failed closed. The new find_runtime_binary logic only treats a non-empty value as authoritative when connector_smoke_runtime_env_was_set reports a matching ${VAR}_WAS_SET flag. The commit added flags only for ENVOY_BIN, TRAEFIK_BIN, and LIGHTTPD_BIN, but HAPROXY_BIN remains a defaulted non-empty variable from common.sh. As a result, when the expected HAPROXY_BIN path is absent, require_local_binary HAPROXY_BIN haproxy now searches broad runtime roots and returns the first executable named haproxy. In a CI or shared build-root setting, a stale or attacker-placed executable can therefore be selected and later run by a connector harness instead of failing with BLOCKED evidence.

title: Phase-1 gap test can be falsely promoted as PASS
description: The patched YAML no longer tries to deny on REQUEST_BODY in phase 1. Instead, phase 1 is only a pass/nolog SecAction, and the actual blocking assertion is moved to a phase-2 SecRule. The expected rule_id is also the phase-2 rule. Because the test still declares phase1 capability and remains in the phase1 case path, a connector that never enforces the phase-1 marker can still pass by blocking in phase 2. The changed limitation text also removes the explicit connector-gap / non-promoted wording. In the reporting path, cases without an explicit non-active metadata classification default to active, and active PASS observations are promotion eligible. The former_xfail flag limits default smoke discovery, but explicit/force-all runtime evidence can still be represented as promotion eligible, creating false assurance about phase-1 request-body handling.

title: RUN_ONE_CASE bypasses connector smoke evidence checks
description: ci/connector-smoke-common.sh now exits with status 0 when the harness returns 0, RUN_ONE_CASE=1, and a non-empty result.json exists. This happens before the existing guard that requires $RESULTS_DIR/<connector>-results.jsonl to be present. The new check does not parse result.json, does not verify that it is for the requested case, and does not verify that it records a passing result. A stale or attacker-created non-empty result.json can therefore make the smoke wrapper return success while no connector-level case evidence was produced. In CI or release workflows that use the smoke command exit status as a quality/security gate, this can create false PASS evidence and hide missing or failed runtime coverage.

title: Unconstrained MRTS paths allow destructive file writes
description: The commit adds MRTS generation/load helpers whose output locations are configurable through exported Make/environment variables. `ci/generate-mrts.sh` creates the selected rule/FTW output directories and then recursively removes `*.conf` and `*.yaml` files below them without checking that those paths are under `tests/mrts/generated` or another disposable build root. `ci/write-mrts-load.sh` similarly accepts `MRTS_LOAD_FILE`, writes a temporary file next to it, and renames it over the requested path. An attacker who can influence these environment variables or Make variables in a CI/build invocation could point them at sensitive writable locations, causing deletion of configuration/YAML files or overwrite/corruption of an arbitrary file. This bypasses the repository's existing pattern of constraining generated build paths and guarding destructive cleanup.

title: Non-promotable runtime evidence is reported as PASS
description: Runtime evidence that is explicitly marked non-promotable is now rendered and counted as ordinary PASS in generated coverage reports. The new normalizer maps any matrix status ending in `_PASS` or `_RESPONSE_BODY_PASS_THROUGH` to `PASS`, which erases the distinction used to prevent XFAIL, pending, future, connector-gap, runtime-difference, and RESPONSE_BODY pass-through evidence from becoming pass evidence. The committed runtime snapshot also contains RESPONSE_BODY rows with `matrix_status: PASS` while simultaneously setting `response_body_non_verified: true`, `runtime_verified: false`, and `promotion_allowed: false`. Generated HAProxy and runtime summary reports then include those rows in PASS counts and PASS details. This is a report-integrity/security-assurance issue: release or coverage decisions could incorrectly conclude that connector response-body or previously non-promotable security cases are verified.

title: RESPONSE_BODY strict aborts can be reported as PASS
description: The new response_body_pass_is_pass_through helper returns false for connection_aborted/aborted transport and for expected/actual statuses other than 200/200. That false value is then passed into matrix_status/semantic_matrix_status as if the case were not RESPONSE_BODY-related. For an active RESPONSE_BODY strict-abort or disruptive blocking case with raw status pass, the computed matrix status therefore becomes plain PASS. update-runtime-snapshot.py persists that value in matrix_status, and generate-case-matrix.py recomputes and overrides matrix_status for any RESPONSE_BODY raw pass row. Later non-promotion fields such as promotion_allowed=false do not prevent PASS status counts and matrix cells from being generated. This undermines the repository's explicit report-integrity invariant that RESPONSE_BODY runtime PASS must not render as plain PASS.

title: HAProxy prepare builds unverified cached source
description: ci/prepare-haproxy-runtime.sh downloads and verifies the official HAProxy tarball, but extract_source() returns immediately when HAPROXY_SOURCE_DIR already exists and REFRESH is not set. The later build step copies and runs make in that existing tree. Because Makefile recipes execute arbitrary shell commands, an attacker who can poison or persist files in the generated SOURCE_ROOT, for example through a shared CI cache, previous build artifact, or writable /src volume, can cause arbitrary code execution while the logs still show that the official archive checksum was verified. The same provenance weakness also appears for an existing HAPROXY_BIN, which is accepted as ready without tying it to the verified source. The helper should either fail on pre-existing source/binary paths unless an explicit trusted local-source mode is enabled, or remove and re-extract into a fresh canonicalized directory before building.

title: ModSecurity v3 commit pin can be omitted from version check
description: The commit adds parsing for ModSecurity v3 approved literals and replaces the generic alias-based ModSecurity v3 release check with check_modsecurity_v3_release_provenance(). However, that new function only calls check_github_release_ref() with MODSECURITY_V3_APPROVED_REPO_URL and MODSECURITY_V3_RELEASE_TAG. MODSECURITY_V3_APPROVED_COMMIT is only added to result.variables for reporting; it is not checked for presence, non-emptiness, SHA-1 commit format, or consistency. Since validate_entries() only reports parsed entries that resolve empty, an entirely missing MODSECURITY_V3_APPROVED_COMMIT line is absent from entries and is not reported. A fixture containing the approved repo and release tag but omitting MODSECURITY_V3_APPROVED_COMMIT returns a successful ModSecurity v3 result when the fake latest release tag matches, validate_entries() returns [], and exit_code() returns 0. This violates the fail-closed provenance boundary for the immutable commit anchor.

title: Python version contract checker no longer parses
description: In ci/checks/security/check-python-version.py, three exception handlers were changed from valid Python 3 syntax, `except (OSError, UnicodeError):`, to invalid syntax, `except OSError, UnicodeError:`. Running `python3 -m py_compile ci/checks/security/check-python-version.py` fails with `SyntaxError: multiple exception types must be parenthesized`. This breaks the Python version contract checker and any workflow or test that imports or executes it. The failure appears fail-closed rather than a bypass of the security contract.

title: Security-data-flow cases break case discovery
description: The new files are placed under tests/cases/security-data-flow, which is part of the normal case discovery tree. However, runner_core.load_case() validates every discovered or explicitly selected case before applicability filtering. The new cases omit the required rules field, declare a new security_data_flow capability that is not in KNOWN_CAPABILITIES, and several also omit the required expect.status integer. As a result, workflows or connector harnesses that list/select/materialize these cases fail with ValueError instead of treating them as pending connector-gap inventory. I confirmed this by running case_cli.py list-cases with --test-case tests/cases/security-data-flow/headers/header_count_limit_exceeded.yaml, which fails with 'case requires rules'.
